rubric.item: Mentions a multicycle-path constraint when the result is only needed every N cycles
rubric.evidence: Multicycle path constraint. Only valid if the path really is used every N cycles

rubric.item: Recommends reading the timing report to find the real critical path (including routing or fanout causes)
rubric.evidence: Before choosing, check the report: Logic vs. route delay split... Fanout on the path

rubric.item: Suggests adding pipeline registers to split the path, accepting extra latency
rubric.evidence: Pipeline the path. Insert registers... Latency goes up by one cycle per stage

rubric.item: Suggests restructuring the logic (for example balancing a chain into a tree or precomputing)
rubric.evidence: Restructure the logic: balanced adder tree, precompute terms that don't depend on the critical input

rubric.item: Mentions retiming (letting the tool move registers)
rubric.evidence: Retime. Let synthesis move existing registers across the logic

rubric.item: Mentions a multicycle-path constraint when the result is only needed every N cycles
rubric.evidence: Multicycle path constraint. Only if the path really is exercised over multiple cycles... set_multicycle_path

rubric.item: Recommends reading the timing report to find the real critical path (including routing or fanout causes)
rubric.evidence: Is it the logic or the routing/fanout? ... Look at the net delay vs cell delay split in the timing report.

rubric.item: Explains that Verilator is 2-state, so X and Z become 0 or 1
rubric.evidence: Verilator is a 2-state, cycle-oriented simulator. It maps every signal to 0 or 1 and has no X or Z.

rubric.item: Says uninitialised registers (missing resets) show up as X only in 4-state simulators
rubric.evidence: a flop without reset looks clean... In a 4-state sim the same flop starts at X

rubric.item: Mentions X-propagation differences (X-optimism or pessimism in if/case statements)
rubric.evidence: An `if (x_sig)` takes the else branch in some simulators and the X handling is pessimistic in others; `case` with X in the selector

rubric.item: Mentions scheduling or race differences (blocking assignments, combinational loops settling)
rubric.evidence: Blocking vs non-blocking races... does not reproduce every zero-delay race... Combinational blocks written with blocking assignments

rubric.item: Recommends running both kinds of simulator or Verilator's X-initialisation randomisation
rubric.evidence: run with `--x-initial unique` plus several seeds, or simulate in a 4-state tool; Lint with both tools

rubric.item: Explains that Verilator is 2-state, so X and Z become 0 or 1
rubric.evidence: Verilator is 2-state and Questa/Icarus are 4-state (0, 1, X, Z); Verilator initialises every variable to 0 (or random)

rubric.item: Says uninitialised registers (missing resets) show up as X only in 4-state simulators
rubric.evidence: A reg that is never reset looks like a valid 0 and the design "works"... In a 4-state sim the reg starts as X

rubric.item: Mentions X-propagation differences (X-optimism or pessimism in if/case statements)
rubric.evidence: `if (X)` is treated as false... `case` with X in the selector can match the default

rubric.item: Mentions scheduling or race differences (blocking assignments, combinational loops settling)
rubric.evidence: Race conditions and scheduling: blocking vs non-blocking mixing, always @* sensitivity

rubric.item: Recommends running both kinds of simulator or Verilator's X-initialisation randomisation
rubric.evidence: run with X-initialisation enabled in Verilator (--x-initial unique); Compare the two runs' waveforms

rubric.item: Explains that Verilator is 2-state, so X and Z become 0 or 1
rubric.evidence: Verilator is a 2-state simulator: every variable is 0 or 1, and X/Z never exist at runtime.

rubric.item: Says uninitialised registers (missing resets) show up as X only in 4-state simulators
rubric.evidence: Registers without reset start at X in 4-state, but at 0 (or a randomised value) in Verilator.

rubric.item: Mentions X-propagation differences (X-optimism or pessimism in if/case statements)
rubric.evidence: In 4-state, `if (x_cond)` takes the else branch, and `case` with X uses the default... X-pessimism on `?:` and `==`

rubric.item: Mentions scheduling or race differences (blocking assignments, combinational loops settling)
rubric.evidence: Race conditions and scheduling: Blocking/non-blocking misuse, combinational loops, and `always @*` sensitivity gaps can behave differently

rubric.item: Recommends running both kinds of simulator or Verilator's X-initialisation randomisation
rubric.evidence: Run with `--x-initial unique` plus several seeds, and compare against a 4-state run.
